newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ACCC, Nine in agreement on court claim.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ACCC, Nine in agreement on court claim.

text.p: Anti-monopolies watchdog the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) said on Monday it had reached an agreement with the Nine Network, a unit of Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd (PBL) over claims the ACCC made in its Federal Court action.
ACCC said that under the agreement Nine's unit Territory Television (NTD8) will terminate the exclusive programme supply agreement with the Seven Network Ltd in relation to the Darwin market.
ACCC said the Nine Network and Territory Television had also agreed it would not enter into any similar agreement with Seven for the purchase of Seven's programming for the Darwin market.
"This will assist the ACCC's objective to substantially increase the programming options for a new entrant in the Darwin market," the ACCC said.

The ACCC had alleged Nine and Seven had breached sections 45 and 47 of the Trade Practices Act by forming exclusive programming arrangements in the Darwin and regional Western Australian TV markets to hinder competition.

ACCC said the Nine Network, Territory Television and Nine director Nicholas Falloon would not contest the ACCC's claims in the proceeding filed on October 24 on the basis that the ACCC withdrew it claims.

It said the Nine Network would give undertakings to the Court that it would terminate the exclusive programme supply agreement with Golden West Network (GWN) if the ACCC won its court claim against GWN for breaching the trade practices act.
GWN is controlled by Kerry Stokes, who is the chairman and largest single shareholder in Seven Network.
ACCC had not reached an agreement with Seven or GWN over its claims in regards to the programming supply arrangements.
At 10.30 a.m. (2330 GMT), Seven shares were three cents lower at A$3.95, while PBL shares were unchanged at A$5.65.
